title: Construction Incidents 2026: What Owners and Contractors Must Do
desc: Building incident or unsafe house: stop work, notify the commune People's Committee within 24 hours, secure the site, assessment, compensation, fines.
summary: The steps investors, contractors, and homeowners must take when a building suffers an incident or shows signs of danger: reporting, securing the site, determining the cause, and compensation under Decree 207/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

Collapsed scaffolding, cracked or collapsed walls, a house that settles and tilts: these are incidents that can occur during construction or while a building is in use. The rules for handling them are in Article 55 of the Construction Law 2025 and Articles 45–48 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP.
h2
1. Risk to safety detected: stop immediately
p
Under Clause 1, Article 55 of the Construction Law 2025, when a risk of an incident affecting lives or neighboring buildings is detected, the investor, contractor, or building owner must:
ul
Promptly stop construction, stop use, and ensure the safety of people and property;
Take measures to limit and prevent danger, and notify the competent authority;
Preserve the scene, except where urgent remedial action is needed to prevent damage.
h2
2. Reporting the incident: immediately and within 24 hours
p
Under Article 45 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP:
ol

Immediately after the incident, by the fastest means, the investor notifies the commune-level People's Committee where it occurred: the name and location of the building, and a preliminary description of the incident and damage.

Within 24 hours, the investor reports in writing to the provincial People's Committee: the name, location, and scale of the building; the parties involved in construction; a description of the incident and its time; and damage to people and property.
If the incident caused harm to people, the report is also sent to the Ministry of Construction and other competent authorities.
p
If the incident occurs while the building is in use, the owner or the person managing or using the building makes the report as above (Clause 5, Article 45).
h2
3. Handling the incident and determining the cause
ul
The investor and contractor carry out search and rescue, ensure safety, and preserve the scene (Clause 1, Article 46).

The provincial People's Committee (or the commune-level People's Committee if authority has been delegated) leads the handling: it decides to stop construction or use, and permits demolition and clearing of the scene after photos, video, and evidence have been collected.
The competent authority establishes an investigation team to determine the cause and assign responsibility (Article 47).
Construction may resume or the building may be used again only when the authority handling the incident permits it (Clause 3, Article 55 of the Law).
p

Assessment costs: for an incident during construction, the investor pays in advance; for an incident during use, the owner pays in advance. Once the result is known, the party that caused the incident must pay these costs (Clause 4, Article 47).
h2
4. Incident records and liability for compensation
p

The investor or owner prepares an incident file including: the site inspection record; relevant design and construction documents; the cause assessment file; and documents on the handling process (Article 48). The organization or individual that caused the incident must compensate for damage and bear the cost of remedying it (Clause 4, Article 55 of the Law; Clause 6, Article 46).
h2
5. An occupied house showing signs of danger
p

If a house has large cracks, is tilting, or is at risk of collapse, the owner must: check the condition, have it assessed (if needed), limit or stop using it, cordon off the area, move people and property, notify the local authority immediately, and repair or demolish as needed (Clause 1, Article 42). Anyone has the right to notify the building owner or the authorities on seeing signs of danger in a building.
h2
6. Failing to report or to preserve the scene is fined
p

Under Article 24 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP, an investor that fails to report or reports late, or fails to prepare the incident file, is fined VND 10–20 million; failing to preserve the scene, clearing it without approval, or failing to remedy the consequences is fined VND 40–60 million (amounts for organizations; individuals pay half under Article 5).
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. When people are injured, first call emergency services and rescue forces; reporting and assessment proceed in parallel following the local authority's instructions.
